newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - Feb 19.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Trading picked up a notch on Tuesday as weather boosted consumption but buyers at all levels of the market remained cautious, Random Lengths said in its midweek review. Lumber prices were flat or showed minor movement in either direction, the reporting agency said.
Traders felt off-balance as they assessed the impact of more Canadian mills faciong fees on shipments to the U.S., Random Lengths said. News of a major curtailment boosted OSB.
Canadian exports as of Feb 11 were 48.5 percent of the Jan-March fee-free quota and 90.4 pct of April-March quota.

Most Western S-P-F prices edged higher through Tuesday. More producers had tighter controls on sales to the U.S. while they developed and employed quota year-end strategies. Std&Btr 2x4 sold mostly in the $410-415 range. The #2&Btr 2x6 lagged and prices were sloppy. Some wide-width suppliers encountered stiffer competition from Hem-Fir, the reporting agency said.

Eastern S-P-F traded at an uneven pace. Most mills held prices or nudged quotes higher. Buyers found occasional deals at slight discounts to published prices. The #1&2 2x4 was a touch stronger and some stud mills reported a slight uptick.

Southern Pine sales got off to a fair start. Fill-in buying predominated and buyers focused more on specified lengths than on random loadings. Most prices held or edged higher, with 2x4 the lone exception; #2 prices slipped $3 central and eastside.
Inland dimension prices were flat. Buyers hesitated at higher quotes for wides; stud precuts sold steadily.

Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir prices held or rose modestly. In Hem-Fir, demand for long lengths was solid. Producers fielded more inquiries for Hem-Fir #2&Btr 2x10, which rose $5. Std&Btr 2x4 strengthened but sold over a wide range. Douglas Fir #2&Btr 2x8&wdr advanced $1-3. Studs were flat.

OSB sales were spotty, but prices firmed on news of Potlatch's plans to curtail three mills for two weeks in early March. A few mills offered shipments next week but several were extended to the week of March 3 or beyond.
